items.title: Shocking secret you won't believe! Emotional arousal in clickbait headlines: An eye-tracking analysis

judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted primarily to examine the levels of emotional arousal evoked by two treatment groups of online news headlines, news and clickbait, compared to a neutral control group.
judge.evidence_topic: The purpose of this paper is to fill a gap in the literature by providing empirical evidence of how clickbait headlines affect online users’ emotional and behavioral responses, specifically emotional arousal and intention to read news.
judge.reason: O artigo relata um experimento empírico sobre os efeitos de manchetes clickbait em usuários de notícias, alinhado ao tema e recorte solicitados. O achado extraído resume fielmente os resultados do resumo: clickbait gera mais excitação que manchetes neutras, mas menos que manchetes de notícia, e a excitação prediz a intenção de ler.

items.title: Effects of Clickbait Headlines on User Responses: An Empirical Investigation

judge.evidence_empirical: An experiment was conducted on two groups of news headlines—traditional news and clickbait— to provide empirical evidence
judge.evidence_topic: This study investigates the influence of a conventional method of delivering news headlines, clickbait, on online users’ perceptions and responses.
judge.reason: O resumo aborda efeitos de clickbait em usuários (tópico). Descreve experimento com dados próprios (empírico). O método extraído (experimento, modelagem de equações estruturais) corresponde ao resumo. O achado é integralmente sustentado pelo resumo: clickbait evoca excitação/curiosidade, curiosidade determina intenção de ler e qualidade percebida determina compartilhamento.

items.title: Exaggerated and Questioning Clickbait Headlines and Their Influence on Media Learning

judge.evidence_empirical: we conducted two online experiments, each testing a 3 (headline-type: accurate, clickbait-question, clickbait-exaggerated) × 2 (exposure: headline-only, full article) factorial. In Study 1, an online sample of US adults ( N = 629) was randomly assigned to one of six news message conditions. Study 2 ( N = 1,674) was a replication study
judge.evidence_topic: To evaluate the impact of clickbait headlines on media learning and article-related beliefs, we conducted two online experiments… an online sample of US adults ( N = 629)… Study 2 ( N = 1,674)
judge.reason: O artigo trata dos efeitos de manchetes clickbait sobre a aprendizagem e crenças de leitores, com experimentos online com adultos dos EUA, sem recorte político. É um estudo empírico com dados próprios. O método extraído (experimentos fatoriais) confere com o resumo. O achado principal extraído (manchete precisa com artigo completo gera melhor reconhecimento/compreensão; correção no texto não anula o efeito negativo) é sustentado literalmente pelo resumo.

items.title: You won't believe it! Truth judgments for clickbait headlines benefit (but less so) from prior exposure

judge.evidence_empirical: In Experiment 1 (N = 241), we hypothesized and found that prior exposure increased the proportion of “true” judgments for both non‐clickbait and clickbait content, but with a reduced effect of prior exposure for statements originally presented in a clickbait format. In Experiment 2 (N = 291), turning to continuous ratings, we found higher truth ratings for repeated than new clickbait statements, even when repetition evidently originated from prior exposure to clickbait statements.
judge.evidence_topic: In two high‐powered experiments, we investigated how prior exposure to statements presented in a clickbait format increases the perceived truth of their content.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda diretamente o efeito de manchetes clickbait em leitores por meio de dois experimentos. O tipo de estudo e o método extraídos batem com o resumo. O achado principal está integralmente sustentado pelo trecho final do resumo: 'exposure to clickbait headlines can increase their content's truth judgments ... although to a lesser extent than for more regular statements'.

items.title: Click me…! The influence of clickbait on user engagement in social media and the role of digital nudging

judge.evidence_empirical: We use a data set of more than 4,400 Facebook posts from 10 different news sources to analyze how clickbait in post headlines and in post text influences user engagement.
judge.evidence_topic: We analyze the impact of clickbait on user interaction on Facebook in the form of liking, sharing and commenting.
judge.reason: O artigo trata dos efeitos de clickbait sobre o engajamento de usuários (likes, compartilhamentos, comentários), o que se enquadra no pedido. É um estudo empírico com dados reais de interação. O método extraído (análise quantitativa de dados de engajamento) confere com o resumo. O achado principal está integralmente apoiado no resumo, que menciona que certas características (pontuação incomum, frases típicas) aumentam a interação e outras a reduzem.

items.title: Emotion Sells: Rage Bait vs. Information Bait in Clickbait News Headlines on Social Media

judge.evidence_empirical: rage bait headlines were linked to higher levels of audience engagement, while information bait was associated with lower engagement.
judge.evidence_topic: This study examined clickbait headlines on social media, focusing on which types of news organizations tend to use this content strategy and whether these strategies effectively drive audience engagement.
judge.reason: O resumo indica claramente que o estudo investiga os efeitos de diferentes tipos de clickbait no engajamento da audiência, tratando do tema do pedido. A descrição do método empírico é compatível com o tipo extraído. O achado extraído é literalmente confirmado pelo resumo.

items.title: Analyzing Sensationalism in News on Twitter (X): Clickbait Journalism by Legacy vs. Online-Native Outlets and the Consequences for User Engagement

judge.evidence_empirical: First, a manual content analysis of 1,440 tweets by news media organizations was conducted, identifying sensationalism through ten features. Second, an automated content analysis was conducted on a dataset of 25,600 tweets, replicating the manual coding process.
judge.evidence_topic: This study empirically investigates whether online-native news outlets utilize more sensational features than legacy news outlets to promote their news stories on Twitter (now X). The impact of sensationalism on subsequent user engagement metrics is also tested.
judge.reason: O artigo analisa empiricalmente a relação entre sensacionalismo (clickbait) em tuítes de veículos jornalísticos e métricas de engajamento de usuários (leitores), com dados próprios de análise de conteúdo.

items.title: Clickbait-style headlines and journalism credibility in Sub-Saharan Africa: Exploring audience perceptions

judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo experimental sobre os efeitos de manchetes clickbait na credibilidade jornalística percebida entre consumidores de notícias online na Zâmbia e Tanzânia, alinhando-se ao pedido. O tipo de estudo, método e achado extraídos são compatíveis com o resumo.

items.title: Aggregation, Clickbait and Their Effect on Perceptions of Journalistic Credibility and Quality

judge.evidence_empirical: This study uses published original and aggregated news articles as stimuli in two online experiments to test readers’ perceptions of news aggregation and clickbait.
judge.evidence_topic: Results also suggest clickbait headlines may lower perceptions of credibility and quality.
judge.reason: O resumo indica que a agregação tem pouco efeito sobre a credibilidade e a qualidade percebidas e que manchetes clickbait podem reduzi-las, sustentando integralmente o achado informado.

items.title: The curiosity effect: Information seeking in the contemporary news environment

judge.evidence_topic: This research investigates how digital news headlines influence contemporary news information seeking.
judge.reason: O achado extraído reflete exatamente o que o resumo afirma: manchetes-resumo elevam a percepção de adequação da informação e a expectativa de engajamento, e são favorecidas na seleção de notícias em sites reais.

judge.evidence_topic: how clickbait headlines influence readers’ clicking behavior and attention allocation

O método extraído (EEG com N2b e P3a) e o achado (manchetes com forward reference atraem mais atenção; tipo de notícia não influenciou) batem integralmente com o resumo.

judge.reason: O resumo menciona explicitamente manchetes clickbait e efeitos na memória, atendendo ao tema. O estudo é experimental, portanto empírico. O método extraído condiz com o resumo. O achado principal está totalmente respaldado pelo trecho sobre edição e memória.

items.title: Seeing is not always believing: an exploratory study of clickbait in WeChat

judge.evidence_empirical: The authors collected longitudinal data in collaboration with a leading company that operates more than 500 WeChat official accounts in China. ... Econometric analysis was employed for empirical validation.
judge.evidence_topic: Headline-level: what characteristics of clickbait headlines attract user clicks
judge.reason: O resumo afirma explicitamente que 'hyperbole, insinuation, and visual rhetoric entice users to click the baited headlines' e que 'there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between the number of clickbait headlines posted by a publisher and its visit traffic', confirmando integralmente o achado extrado.

items.title: Did clickbait crack the code on virality?

judge.evidence_empirical: Using a controlled experiment, we confirm that high-emotional headlines are shared more and show evidence that clickbait often leads to inferences of manipulative intent and source derogation. We then use a well-known secondary data set containing 19,386 articles from 27 leading online publishers. We supplement it with Twitter share data, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and additional control variables.
judge.evidence_topic: Although clickbait is a ubiquitous tactic in digital media, we challenge the popular belief that clickbait systematically leads to enhanced sharing of online content on social media. Using the Persuasion Knowledge Model, we predict that clickbait tactics may be perceived by some readers as a manipulative attempt, leading to source derogation where the publisher may be perceived as less competent and trustworthy. This, in turn, may reduce some readers’ intention to share content.
judge.reason: O artigo claramente trata dos efeitos de manchetes clickbait sobre leitores (compartilhamento) e é um estudo empírico com dados de leitores (experimento) e de engajamento (dados de Twitter). O método extraído, porém, descreve apenas a análise de dados secundários e omite o experimento controlado, o que não confere com o resumo. O achado principal está correto, pois o resumo confirma que artigos clickbait geram menos compartilhamentos e que o resultado se mantém com controle de seleção endógena.
